Measured (`GC_MODE=software playwright test --project gc --grep "connected-terrain clean" --repeat-each 8 --workers 1`, this machine): a tight 80.50-80.52 B/frame attributed across 8 clean runs. 0016 §1's ordinary margin convention (`ceil(measured) + 8 B`): ceil(80.52) = 81, + 8 = 89 -- not widened to avoid ADR 0029's own failure mode (M13b: a margin wide enough to swallow the `object` control's own stable ~16 B/frame stops it tripping), since 89 already sits 7.5 B below the control's own reading (below). `object` control on `main` measured a constant 96.50 B/frame attributed across 4 repeats (clean's own 80.5 + 16.0, ADR 0029's own figure exactly) -- verified still tripping at 89 (8/8 repeats: `neg object main` reports `pass` for the expected-mismatch verdict, i.e. `B.main` reads `false` as required). `burst` control on `main` verified still tripping (3/3 repeats, `@slow`; a multi-KB burst is nowhere near this margin). `client`/`sim`/`gen0` are unaffected by this round (ADR 0029, no software row for them) and their own hardware rows are unchanged.

0016 §1's formula, connected-terrain's own shape (a real WebGPU adapter, the 110 B floor applies): ceil(measured clean) + 8 B margin, no attribution. First measured against class "budgeted" pre-emptively (a dispatched action's own result is JSON-parsed on main, which allocates by construction -- gc-slice.ts's own module comment) without first trying "strict"; on review, re-measured against "strict" instead -- clean and every negative control (object main, burst main included) pass 8/8 -- so this row is "strict" like every other page's main: the ~1,296 B/600 frames pollActionResults@client-* adds (20 dispatches at DISPATCH_EVERY_FRAMES=30, ~65 B/parse) is real allocation but too small to cross V8's young-generation scavenge threshold, the same reason connected-terrain's own ~102 B/frame triggers no GC event either. Measured (playwright test --project gc --grep "zero_gc_action clean" --repeat-each 8 --workers 1, this machine): 106.59-106.92 B/frame across 8 clean runs (windowByFn: draw@terrain 28800 B, drain@terrain 12000 B, stepFrame@client 7200 B -- connected-terrain's own three sites, unchanged -- plus pollActionResults@client-* ~1296 B, the one new site). ceil(106.92) = 107, + 8 B margin = 115 -- only 4 B above connected-terrain's own 111, confirming the action path itself costs little. **M16b re-attribution (coordinator gate):** giving fixtures/puts a real type Ui = PutsUi made this page's own main rise to 112.06-112.51 B/frame (still under 115, headroom narrowed from ~8 B to ~2.5 B) -- gc-slice.ts ticks the sim once per measured frame (600 real ticks), crossing Puts::tick's own 20-tick Global.day boundary about 30 times in the window, each a real kind-1 Ui record client.ts's pollActionResults now parses on main (inherent to this milestone's feature, not a bug: windowByFn named a new subarray@:0 entry at 3000 B and pollActionResults@client-* at 2448-2668 B, versus ~1296 B pre-M16b). One real inefficiency found and fixed inside that: the drain used to TextDecoder.decode() every kind-1 record it popped, including one a later record in the same drain immediately overwrites (coalesced away, Planning decisions: "coalesced to the newest value per rAF") -- client.ts now copies only raw bytes per record (copyBytes, no allocation) and decodes the winning one once, after the walk. Re-measured post-fix (playwright test --project gc --grep "zero_gc_action clean" --repeat-each 8 --workers 1): 108.2-108.44 B/frame (windowByFn: subarray@:0 down to 1260 B, pollActionResults@client-* down to 2088 B) -- back within ~1.5 B of the pre-M16b baseline, comfortably under 115 (~6.6 B headroom, close to the original ~8 B). ceil(108.44) = 109, + 8 B margin = 117 -- higher than the existing 115, but not applied: the measured max already fits 115 with real margin, and 0029's "never widen without a reason" cuts against raising a budget the current code does not need. object main re-verified tripping (8/8 repeats) at the unchanged 115.
